scenes.title: Inside the cramped MRI bore: volunteer tells the intercom 'the scanner is pleasant' as dACC conflict spikes
scenes.era: 2009, UC Davis / Carnegie Mellon 3-Tesla fMRI neuroimaging suite

layout.description: Bright clinical MRI suite split by an observation window: inside the scanner room, a volunteer lies tightly fitted inside the cylindrical white 3-Tesla MRI bore wearing ear defenders and speaking into a fiber-optic intercom microphone ('The scanner was comfortable'); in the control room foreground, Vincent van Veen watches the live brain monitor light up at the midline conflict detector.

positions.who: Free-choice volunteer (mannequin in blue hospital scrubs on the MRI bed)
positions.where: lying supine inside the narrow cylindrical 3T MRI bore speaking into the intercom mic
positions.facing: facing upward inside the scanner tunnel

positions.who: Neuroscientist Vincent van Veen (mannequin in collared shirt and lab coat)
positions.where: seated at the control-room glass window before the real-time fMRI activation console
positions.facing: watching both the volunteer through the window and the sagittal dACC activation map

positions.where: seated in the hallway alcove listening on an intercom speaker

props.name: 3-Tesla cylindrical fMRI scanner bore
props.period_detail: large clinical white MRI magnet with sliding patient table and head coil
props.physical_behavior: houses the cramped volunteer during the noisy 45-minute session

props.name: fiber-optic scanner intercom microphone
props.period_detail: non-magnetic white plastic microphone clipped inside the head coil
props.physical_behavior: carries the volunteer's reluctant 'It is very comfortable' endorsement

props.name: control-room sagittal brain monitor
props.period_detail: widescreen neuroimaging console displaying midline dorsal anterior cingulate and anterior insula activation
props.physical_behavior: warm amber-gold subsurface glow highlights the midline conflict region during free-choice trials

actions.verb_sequence: winces slightly inside the tight MRI head coil -> speaks 'The scanner is pleasant' into the intercom mic
points to the sharp dorsal anterior cingulate activation peak on the control-room screen

reactions.reaction: exhales and relaxes tension once his post-scan rating shifts upward
logs the r > 0.55 correlation between the midline spike and the flipped comfort score

scenes.wardrobe: Volunteer in light-blue cotton MRI-safe scrubs; researchers in white lab coat over Oxford shirt.
scenes.lighting: High-key clinical daylight across both the MRI bay and glass-walled control room.
scenes.recognition_hook: Lying cramped inside a loud MRI tube and telling the next patient 'it's super comfortable' made the brain's conflict alarm light up — and rewrote their real opinion.

key_visual.description: the volunteer lies inside the narrow MRI scanner speaking into an intercom while the control-room monitor shows midline brain conflict

scenes.title: Paid control condition: external bonus keeps the conflict alarm quiet

layout.description: MRI prep desk where a paid-condition volunteer signs a bonus payment receipt envelope before reading the exact same script with a calm, unchanged brain trace.

positions.where: standing at the prep counter signing a bonus payment voucher envelope
handing over the printed bonus voucher envelope

props.name: printed bonus payment voucher envelope
props.period_detail: crisp white university payment voucher clearly marked 'Extra Scripted Reading Bonus'
props.physical_behavior: gives a clear external reason so the volunteer later still rates the scanner uncomfortable

actions.verb_sequence: accepts the bonus voucher envelope -> reads the script calmly -> later circles 'Unpleasant' honestly on the exit rating

reactions.reaction: notes the flat dACC trace and unchanged honest rating

scenes.recognition_hook: Give someone an extra payment excuse to read the exact same words, and their conflict alarm stays quiet — so their true opinion never budges.

scenes.title: Post-scan comfort rating flip

layout.description: Bright debriefing table outside the MRI bay where the free-choice volunteer circles a high comfort score on the post-scan questionnaire.

positions.where: seated at the debriefing desk circling 6 out of 7 for scanner comfort
comparing pre- vs post-scan score sheets

props.name: 1-to-7 scanner comfort rating scale
props.period_detail: printed questionnaire from 1 (Extremely Uncomfortable) to 7 (Very Pleasant)
props.physical_behavior: pen circles a high pleasantness number matching the earlier dACC spike

actions.verb_sequence: nods earnestly and circles a pleasant rating on the paper scale

reactions.reaction: matches the high comfort score directly to that volunteer's scanner trace

scenes.recognition_hook: The bigger the conflict spike inside the tube, the more genuinely the volunteer liked the tube ten minutes later.

scenes.title: Everyday rationalization after an overpriced choice

layout.description: Sunlit sidewalk outside a tiny crowded café with a long queue where a diner praises a tiny pastry to friends.

positions.where: holding a tiny plate after a 90-minute wait, gesturing enthusiastically
glancing from the tiny plate to the long line

props.name: tiny porcelain plate and long velvet queue rope
props.period_detail: minimalist café plate beside a '90 MIN WAIT' sign
props.physical_behavior: diner gestures proudly over the tiny portion

actions.verb_sequence: steps out of the 90-minute line -> holds up the tiny pastry -> nods insistently about how amazing it was

reactions.reaction: exchange knowing glances at classic dissonance reduction

scenes.recognition_hook: Wait 90 minutes by your own free choice, and your anterior cingulate will make sure that tiny pastry tastes incredible.
